```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(rminka)
library(sf)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)

```

```{r cached-observations, eval=TRUE}
cached_obs <- utils::read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "vignette_observations.csv", package = "rminka"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
cached_obs$observed_on <- as.Date(cached_obs$observed_on)
```
This document introduces the basic tools in `rminka` and shows how to use them
to retrieve and process biodiversity data. The API examples are shown as code
but are not run while the vignette is built. The local examples use a small,
synthetic dataset included with the package so that the vignette can be built
without network access.

After installing the package, read `vignette("introduction-to-rminka")` to learn
more.


### <u>- Project Queries </u>

Project-related functions will be illustrated using the project Biomarató Tarragona 2025.

### ● `mnk_proj_byname()`

Initially, only the project name is known, so a search is performed to retrieve the corresponding project ID. This is done with `mnk_proj_byname()`. Here we use the query "biomarato 2025".

```{r project1, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
prj_names <- mnk_proj_byname("biomarato 2025")

prj_names 

# For this example 

prj_names[,c(1:2)]

```
### ● `mnk_proj_info()`
 
Once the project ID is known, detailed information can be retrieved with `mnk_proj_info()`. For the Biomarató Tarragona 2025, the project ID is 419.

```{r project_info, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
prj_info <- mnk_proj_info(419)

prj_info

```
### ● `mnk_proj_user()`

Users explicitly subscribed to a project can be retrieved with `mnk_proj_user()` using the project ID

```{r project_info_user, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
prj_user <- mnk_proj_user(419)

prj_user

```
Note: The simplest way to retrieve all participants in a project — including those who are not subscribed — is to download the project's observations with `mnk_proj_obs()` and then extract the unique values of user_login. Each observation includes the observer's login, so the set of distinct logins corresponds to the project's participants.

If the project lasts only one year, or if you are only interested in the participants from a single month, a single function call is sufficient. For example, project 419 ran in 2025, so all its observations can be obtained with `mnk_proj_obs(419, year = 2025)`:

```{r project_info_user2, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
# 1. Download all observations for the project in may 2025

obs_2025 <- mnk_proj_obs(419,year=2025, month = 5, quiet = TRUE)

# 2. Extract the unique participants

participants_may_2025 <- obs_2025 %>%
  distinct(user_login) %>%
  arrange(user_login)

participants_may_2025

```


### ● `mnk_proj_obs()`

Returns all observations for a project within a selected year, and optionally within a specific month. For the Biomarató Tarragona 2025 (project ID 419), observations for the entire year are obtained with `mnk_proj_obs(419, year = 2025)`, while observations for a single month — for example, May — are obtained with `mnk_proj_obs(419, year = 2025, month = 5)`.

```{r project_obs_proj, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
prj_obs <- mnk_proj_obs(419, year= 2025, month=5)

prj_obs[2:14]

```


### <u>- User Queries</u>  

User-related functions will be illustrated using the user Xavier Salvador.
  
### ● `mnk_user_byname()`
 
Initially, only an approximate name is known, so a search is performed to retrieve the corresponding user_login. For this example, we start with the query "xavi", which returns a list of possible logins. The desired user — Xavier Salvador — is then selected from that list.

```{r user_name, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
user_name <- mnk_user_byname("xavi")

user_name

```


### ● `mnk_user_info()`
 
Once the user ID is known, detailed information can be retrieved with mnk_user_info(). For Xavier Salvador (login "xasalva"), the user ID is 4
   
```{r user_info, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
user_info <- mnk_user_info(4)

user_info

```


### ● `mnk_user_proj()`
 
 `mnk_user_proj()` returns the projects to which a user is explicitly subscribed, given the user ID. For Xavier Salvador (user ID 4), the list is obtained with `mnk_user_proj(4)`.

Note: Projects in which a user has contributed observations but is not formally subscribed cannot be retrieved directly in R.
 
```{r user_project, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
user_project <- mnk_user_proj(4)

user_project

```


### ● `mnk_user_obs()`
 
Returns all observations for a user within a selected year, and optionally within a specific month. For Xavier Salvador (user ID 4), observations for the entire year are obtained with `mnk_user_obs(4, year = 2025)`, while observations for a single month, for example May, are obtained with `mnk_user_obs(4, year = 2025, month = 5)`.

```{r user_obs, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
user_obs <- mnk_user_obs(user_id= 4, year = 2025, month = 8)

user_obs

```


### <u>- Place Queries</u>

Place-related functions will be illustrated using the place  Piscines del Fòrum
 
### ● `mnk_place_byname()`
 
Initially, only an approximate place name is known, so a search is performed to retrieve the corresponding place ID. For this example, we start with the query "forum", which returns a list of possible places. The project actually uses "Piscinas del Forum", which does not match the initial assumption, so it is recommended to try several searches with different terms until the desired place is identified.

```{r place_name, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
places <- mnk_place_byname("Forum")

places[,1:6]

```

### ● `mnk_place_sf()`
 
Returns the sf geometry for a place given its place ID. Once the place ID is known, the geometry can be retrieved with `mnk_place_sf()`. For Piscinas del Forum, the geometry is obtained with `mnk_place_sf(253)`.

The API example displays the returned geometry with Leaflet. The function
returns an `sf` object in WGS 84 (EPSG:4326), including the place name as an
attribute.

```{r place_sf, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
# 1. Downloading the geometry 

places_forum <- mnk_place_sf(253)

# 2. Drawing the map

 forum_sf <-leaflet(places_forum) %>%
                addProviderTiles("providers$CartoDB.Positron", group = "OSM") %>%
                addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldImagery", group = "Satellite") %>%
                addPolygons(
                  color = "#2c4fb8",
                  weight = 2,
                  opacity = 1,
                  fillOpacity = 0.4,
                  label = ~name, # information added from previous function
                  highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 3, bringToFront = TRUE)
                ) %>%
                addLayersControl(baseGroups = c("Satellite", "OSM"))
 forum_sf
```

```{r cached-place-geometry, eval=TRUE}
places_forum <- sf::st_read(
  system.file("extdata", "espigo_w.shp", package = "rminka"),
  quiet = TRUE
)

ggplot2::ggplot(places_forum) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(fill = "lightblue", color = "navy") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

### ● `mnk_place_obs()`

Returns all observations recorded within a place during a selected year and,
optionally, month. The result is a data frame without geometry. For Piscines
del Fòrum, observations for February 2025 can be retrieved with
`mnk_place_obs(place_id = 253, year = 2025, month = 2)`.

Although the output has no geometry, it can be converted to an `sf` object with the helper function `mnk_obs_sf()`. The resulting points can then be mapped with `ggplot2`.

```{r places_obs, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
obs_place <- mnk_place_obs(place_id = 253, year = 2025, month = 2, quiet = TRUE)

obs_place
```

```{r cached-place-observations, eval=TRUE}
obs_place <- subset(cached_obs, taxon_name %in% c(
  "Diplodus sargus", "Parablennius pilicornis"
))
```

The following local example converts the cached observations to an `sf` object
and maps them with the packaged study-area polygon.

```{r cached-place-map, eval=TRUE}
obs_sf <- mnk_obs_sf(
  obs_place, id, taxon_name, observed_on, user_login, quality_grade
)

ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = places_forum, fill = "lightblue", color = "navy") +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = obs_sf, color = "red", size = 2) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

### <u>- Observation Queries</u>

### ●`mnk_obs_id()`
 
Returns a single observation given its observation ID. This function is seldom used in practice, as observation IDs are not usually known beforehand.

```{r obs_id, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
obs_id <- mnk_obs_id(id = 553028)

obs_id

```

### ● `mnk_obs()`
 
 This is the core function of the package. It supports searches by project,
 user, place, date, week number, taxon, or geographic area. Two important notes
 apply to all `mnk_obs()` calls:

When the query is executed, a message reports the total number of observations found. If this number exceeds 10,000, only the first 10,000 are downloaded by default. To retrieve all records, set `limit_download = FALSE`.

To retrieve only validated records, use `quality = "research"`. Previous
examples covered searches by project, user, and place; the following examples
show searches by taxon and bounding box.

a) <u>Taxon search</u>. The following examples search for the genus Raja in
2025 and the species Raja brachyura in 2023.

```{r obs, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE}
# Suppress console messages in this example with `quiet = TRUE`.

# Get observations for genus Raja in 2025 by user Xavier Salvador ( user_id=4)

obs <- mnk_obs(taxon_name = "Raja", year = 2025, user_id = 4, quiet = TRUE, 
               quality = "research")

obs # show full dataframe

# Get observations for species Raja brachyura in 2023 by user Xasalva (user_id= 4)

obs_brachyura <- mnk_obs(taxon_name = "Raja brachyura", year = 2023, user_id = 4, 
                         quiet = TRUE, quality = "research")

obs_brachyura[, c(1,2, 10, 11, 16, 27)]  # show selected columns

```
Images from observations can be displayed with the `magick` package by using
the observation's `url_picture`, as shown below.

```{r brachyura-pic, echo=TRUE, out.width='85%', fig.align='center', fig.alt="Raja undulata observed by Xavier Salvador"}
# Get observations for the species Raja undulata in 2022 by user Xasalva (user_id = 4).

obs_undulata <- mnk_obs(taxon_name = "Raja undulata", year = 2022, user_id = 4, 
                         quiet = TRUE, quality = "research")

# select 3rd observation and get picture URL (url_picture)

url_pic_undulata <- as.character(obs_undulata$url_picture[3])

# read image directly from URL

img_undulata <- image_read(url_pic_undulata )

  # add copyright caption at top
  img_undulata <- image_annotate(
    img_undulata,
    "© Xavier Salvador",
    size = 10, 
    gravity = "northwest", 
    color = "white", 
  ) 

# display image in the document

img_undulata

```

b) <u>Bounding-box search</u>. Observations within a rectangular area are retrieved by supplying the coordinates of the southwest and northeast corners. For example, to search around Platja de Sant Sebastià in Barcelona, define the bounding box and pass it to `mnk_obs()`.

```{r obs_1, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
# Read the packaged study-area shapefile.

shp <- system.file("extdata", "espigo_w.shp", package = "rminka")

espigo <- sf::st_read(shp, quiet = TRUE)

# Transform the study area to WGS 84.

bounds <- st_transform(espigo, 4326)

```
Similarly, the area can also be defined by a vector from two points, Pmax and Pmin, 
where the area is defined as:

`bounds <- c(ymax, xmax, ymin, xmin)`

Applied to the Espigó del W example, this would be:

`bounds <-c(41.371239, 2.193971, 41.368182, 2.189147)`

The two points, Pmax and Pmin, will be displayed with the study area of Espigó
del W in a static map to illustrate the bounding-box coordinates.

```{r bounds-api, eval=FALSE}
obs_torpedo_bounds <- mnk_obs(
  taxon_name = "Torpedo", year = 2024, bounds = bounds,
  quality = "research", quiet = TRUE
)
```

```{r bounds, include = TRUE , echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
# Southwest corner
xmin <- 2.189147
ymin <- 41.368182

# Northeast corner
xmax <- 2.193971
ymax <- 41.371239

pts <- data.frame(
  id = c("Pmin", "Pmax"),
  lng = c(xmin, xmax),
  lat = c(ymin, ymax)
)

points_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(pts, coords = c("lng", "lat"), crs = 4326)

obs_torpedo_bounds <- subset(cached_obs, taxon_name == "Torpedo torpedo")

obs_bounds_sf <- mnk_obs_sf(
  obs_torpedo_bounds, id, taxon_name, observed_on, user_login, quality_grade
)

ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = bounds, fill = "lightblue", color = "navy") +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = points_sf, color = "blue", size = 2) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = obs_bounds_sf, color = "red", size = 2) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```


### ● `mnk_obs_byday()`
 
Works like `mnk_obs()` but uses an explicit date interval instead of year or month parameters. The interval is defined by:

`d1`: start date in 'yyyy-mm-dd' format
`d2`: end date in 'yyyy-mm-dd' format

```{r obs_byday, include = TRUE ,echo=TRUE}
# Retrieve Raja undulata observations by Xasalva (user_id = 4) between 2024-01-01 and 2024-05-25.

obs_undulata_2024 <- mnk_obs_byday(taxon_name = "Raja undulata", d1 = "2024-01-01", 
                             d2= "2024-05-25", quiet = TRUE, quality = "research")

obs_undulata_2024

```


### ● `mnk_obs_update()`
 
Downloads observations from the Minka API filtered by the date they were last updated. It's the best way to keep a local database in sync without re-downloading everything. The date they were last updated  is `day_update` in 'yyyy-mm-dd' format.

```{r obs_update, include = TRUE ,echo=TRUE}
# Retrieve Raja undulata observations by Xasalva (user_id = 4), updated since 2024-01-01.

obs_undulata_2024_updated <- mnk_obs_update(day_update = "2024-01-01", taxon_name = "Raja undulata", 
                             quiet = TRUE, quality = "research")

obs_undulata_2024_updated

```

### <u>- Auxiliary functions</u>

The examples below show how the helper functions work. The first two use the *Torpedo torpedo* observations at the Espigó Hotel W from the previous sections. The last two use separate, specific examples.

### ● `mnk_obs_sf()`

This function converts an observations data frame into a spatial layer in sf format.
The function takes the latitude/longitude columns returned by `mnk_obs` or by any other function in the rminka package that returns an observations data frame — such as `mnk_proj_obs` or `mnk_user_obs` — and converts them into an sf POINT layer. By default the geometry is returned in CRS EPSG:4326 (WGS84), but you can specify any CRS you need via the crs argument.
Its basic usage has already been shown briefly in previous sections. Here we develop a detailed example using the *Torpedo torpedo* observations at the espigó Hotel W.

```{r sf_obs, include = TRUE ,echo=TRUE,message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
obs_utm <- mnk_obs_sf(obs_torpedo_bounds, id, taxon_name,
                      observed_on, user_login, quality_grade, url_picture,
                      uri, crs = 25831)

ggplot2::ggplot(obs_utm) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(color = "red", size = 2) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Synthetic observations in ETRS89 / UTM zone 31N",
    x = "Easting (m)",
    y = "Northing (m)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

### ● `export_mnk_qgis()`

This function writes one or more `sf` objects to a GeoPackage (`.gpkg`), creating one layer per object. It is designed for a smooth GIS workflow, especially with QGIS: it ensures valid geometries, drops Z/M dimensions, removes list-columns that GDAL cannot write, and transforms features to the target CRS.

We will apply it to the two examples from the previous section.

```{r export_mnk, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, echo=TRUE}
export_mnk_qgis(
  observations = obs_utm,
  file = file.path(tempdir(), "shape")
)

# The .gpkg extension is added automatically.

# The function can also export several layers to the same GeoPackage:

export_mnk_qgis(
  place_area = places_forum,
  observations = obs_sf,
  file = file.path(tempdir(), "forum")
)

```
### ● `get_wrm_tax()`

This function downloads taxonomic information from the World Register of Marine Species [(WoRMS)](https://www.marinespecies.org/) for a given scientific name.
Two examples illustrate its use with observation data: one retrieves taxonomy
for a single species, and the other retrieves taxonomy for each species in a
community.

```{r get_taxonom_mnk, eval=FALSE}
# First example: a single species

get_wrm_tax("Diplodus sargus")

# Second example: retrieve taxonomy for every species in the observations.

taxon_unic <- obs_place %>%
  filter(!is.na(taxon_name)) %>%
  distinct(taxon_name) %>%
  pull(taxon_name)

taxonomy_df <- map_dfr(
  setNames(taxon_unic, taxon_unic),  
  ~ get_wrm_tax(.x),
  .id = "taxon_name"
)

obs_place_tax <- obs_place %>%
  left_join(taxonomy_df, by = "taxon_name")

```

For an offline demonstration of joining taxonomy data, use a small local table:

```{r cached-taxonomy, eval=TRUE}
taxonomy_df <- data.frame(
  taxon_name = c("Diplodus sargus", "Parablennius pilicornis"),
  kingdom = "Animalia"
)
obs_place_tax <- dplyr::left_join(obs_place, taxonomy_df, by = "taxon_name")
```

### ● `shrt_name()`

This function creates a standardized abbreviation from a scientific name. The
following example uses it to plot observation frequencies for the species in
the `obs_place` data frame.

```{r shrt_name, include=TRUE, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE}
#Create standardized abbreviations for scientific names

obs_place <- obs_place %>%
  mutate(
    shrt_tax_name = map_chr(taxon_name, ~ {
      if (is.na(.x) || .x == "") NA_character_ else shrt_name(.x)
    })
  )
  
#Count observations per abbreviated species and keep top 10

freq_top10 <- obs_place %>%
  filter(!is.na(shrt_tax_name)) %>%          # remove missing names
  count(shrt_tax_name, name = "n_obs") %>%    # count occurrences
  slice_max(n_obs, n = 10) %>%                # keep the 10 most frequent
  arrange(n_obs)   

#Plot horizontal bar chart of observation frequency

ggplot(freq_top10, aes(x = n_obs, y = reorder(shrt_tax_name, n_obs))) +
        geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
        geom_text(aes(label = n_obs), hjust = -0.2, size = 2) +  # add n as label
        scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +  # make room for labels
        labs(
              x = "Number of observations",
              y = "Species (abbreviated)",
              title = "Observation frequency",
              subtitle = " Forum February 2025"
            ) +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```
